name: Luxembourg

findings.reversal_of: Huawei radio access network at Proximus Luxembourg
findings.summary: Proximus Luxembourg, reported to run an all-Huawei radio access network, chose Nokia to replace its incumbent RAN vendor under a seven-year 5G deal announced December 2020, mirroring Proximus's Belgian swap.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal of an operational (tier 5) Huawei 4G RAN. Neither company gave a security reason; Light Reading notes the PM had urged operators to weigh 'geostrategic sensitivity' and that Luxembourg had not banned Huawei. Coded commercial on stated reasons; reviewer may judge geopolitical. Completion of the swap not confirmed in opened sources.

findings.summary: Proximus Luxembourg signed a seven-year deal for Nokia AirScale radio equipment covering indoor and outdoor 5G coverage, with Ericsson supplying the 5G core, replacing Huawei in the radio network.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finland) and Ericsson (Sweden) are EU/Nordic vendors, so pole third. Contract value not disclosed. Rollout was due to start in 2021; current status not checked.

findings.summary: Light Reading reported that state-owned incumbent POST Luxembourg had not previously used Chinese vendors and kept Ericsson for its 5G radio network.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S2 source, so uncorroborated; tier 3 assumed for a continuing vendor relationship, no award notice seen. Note LUX-005: POST does run Huawei enterprise routers elsewhere in its network, so 'no Chinese vendors' applies at most to the radio network.

findings.summary: Orange Luxembourg, which analysts at Strand Consult said relied fully on Huawei for its 4G radio network, selected Nokia for its 5G network, per Light Reading.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S2 source relaying Strand Consult; no Orange or Nokia release opened. Whether Orange's Huawei 4G RAN was also removed is not established, so no reversal coded.

findings.summary: A denial-of-service attack exploiting an undocumented flaw in Huawei enterprise routers used by POST Luxembourg caused a nationwide outage of over three hours on 23 July 2025, hitting fixed, mobile and emergency calls.
findings.analyst_inference: Both opened sources relay The Record's reporting, so not independent; not corroborated. Evidences Huawei routing equipment operational in the national incumbent's network. still_current true: POST's CEO said (Paperjam, ~Sept 2026) it would not exclude a supplier without an explicit regulatory requirement. Which network segment the routers serve is not established.

findings.local_actor: Commune of Bissen / Ministry of the Economy
findings.reversal_of: Google hyperscale data centre project at Bissen (land acquired 2017)
findings.summary: Google's planned EUR 1bn Bissen data centre, on land bought in 2017 and rezoned after a court challenge, stalled: Google missed environmental and permit steps, ministers said the decision lay with Google, and no construction has started.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a pause, not a cancellation: no source opened shows Google formally abandoning the project. Tier 3 = completed land purchase from a state-arranged sale; no construction. Reason coded commercial: the minister suspected Google's 'new strategic considerations' amid Belgian expansion; zoning and litigation also delayed it. EUR 1bn announced value not converted (no source-date rate). Status in 2025-26 not established, so still_current null.

findings.financier: EuroHPC JU (50%, Digital Europe Programme); remainder not stated
findings.summary: EuroHPC signed the contract for MeluXina-AI: 252 nodes, 1,008 liquid-cooled Nvidia GB200 NVL4 Blackwell GPUs, integrated by E4 Computer Engineering with Dell servers, EUR 80m total budget, half EU-funded, installation from autumn 2026 in Bissen.
findings.analyst_inference: Accelerator vendor Nvidia sets pole us; integrator E4 (Italy) and Dell (US) noted. Luxinnovation (Dec 2024) cited 'more than 2,100' GPU accelerators at selection, versus 1,008 GPUs in the signed contract; the contract figure is used. Luxinnovation does not name the vendor, so it does not corroborate the Nvidia award; single opened S1 permits medium. EUR 80m is a budget, not a contract price; not converted.

findings.local_actor: Government of Luxembourg (Prime Minister; ministries of economy, digitalisation, defence, research)
findings.summary: Luxembourg signed a multi-year strategic partnership with French firm Mistral AI covering public-service AI adoption, defence, and research, with Mistral opening a local office and solutions hosted locally under state data control.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: a framework partnership; the government page does not call it binding. Mistral is French, so pole third. Local hosting suggests on-premise deployment, but who holds the weights is not established, so not coded domestic.

findings.local_actor: Luxembourg Ministry of Defence / Luxembourg Armed Forces
findings.summary: Under the Mistral partnership, Luxembourg's Defence Ministry signed a separate contract with Mistral AI to integrate AI tools into the armed forces' activities.
findings.analyst_inference: Signed contract with named counterparty; value and scope not disclosed. Same announcement as LUX-008; bundled.

findings.local_actor: Clarence (JV of Proximus and state-owned LuxConnect)
findings.summary: Proximus and state-owned LuxConnect launched Clarence, a joint venture offering Google Distributed Cloud Hosted, a disconnected sovereign cloud run from Belgian and Luxembourg facilities and aimed at governments and regulated firms.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us on the equipment rule: Google supplies the software stack and its updates, though the disconnected design removes run-time connectivity to Google; reviewer may prefer null. Year 2023 inferred from 'Wednesday, October 25' and the March 2023 Proximus-Google deal. Customers and ownership split not stated. Cloud is a global layer; coded here because Clarence is not a public cloud region.

applications.null_reason: budget spent on networks, facilities and models leads; no surveillance or e-government AI vendor evidence surfaced

research_gaps: Has Google formally abandoned or sold back the Bissen land (state right of first refusal), and when? No 2025-26 status found.
Which segment of POST Luxembourg's network uses Huawei routers, and did the ILR or government order any vendor review after the July 2025 outage?
Has Orange Luxembourg removed Huawei from its 4G RAN, and was the Proximus Luxembourg Huawei swap completed?
Does the Mistral deployment run on state-controlled infrastructure (e.g. MeluXina or government data centres) with locally held weights?
Government sovereign cloud: DCD reports a 'Luxembourg govt launches sovereign cloud' item not reviewed; who supplies its stack? Any Microsoft sovereign-cloud deal?
MeluXina (2021) system vendor and Nvidia content not coded; check the 2,100 vs 1,008 GPU discrepancy for MeluXina-AI.
